tagline.text: Meeting whale sharks in Sogod Bay, Southern Leyte, naturally and without feeding

location.label: Location
location.text: Son-ok village, Pintuyan, Southern Leyte, on the southwest of Panaon Island in Sogod Bay

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May (opens in October, closes in early June)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: One night or more (the encounter itself takes about 3 hours)

children.text: Pintuyan is a town on the southwest of Panaon Island where visitors meet whale sharks (locally called butanding) in Sogod Bay without feeding. The season runs from October or November to May, and local fisherman-turned-spotters guide you by boat.
Pintuyan is a small town at the southwestern end of Panaon Island in Southern Leyte, with a population of about
in the 2024 census. Travelers know it because whale sharks visit Sogod Bay each season and can be seen up close. In the Philippines, whale sharks are called butanding.

Its biggest feature is that there is no feeding. Unlike Oslob in Cebu or Bohol, where food is scattered to keep whale sharks in one place, local spotters here find whale sharks that rise to the surface when plankton and small crustaceans gather. That means luck is involved, and many visitors say the moment feels all the more special for it. Some sources group Pintuyan with Donsol (Bicol) because the two operate in a similar way.

The operation is led by local fishermen. According to news reports, the municipal government started whale shark tourism in the mid-2000s and set rules by ordinance in 2009. The Son-ok spotters and guides association reportedly has about
trained fishermen. Roughly
visitors came from October 2025 to late May 2026, up from about 2,040 in 2023, 3,894 in 2024 and 6,521 in 2025.

Pintuyan is not easy to reach from Manila and the season is limited, so it takes planning, but combined with the diving, snorkeling and marine parks around Sogod Bay it makes a rewarding 3–4 day trip. Season details and fees change from year to year, so it is safest to check with the Pintuyan tourism office before you go. For first-time visitors, here is our advice. Pintuyan is not a day-trip destination; stay at least a night and plan around the weather and whale shark news. The day before, ask the tourism office or your lodging about recent sightings, sleep in town and book an afternoon encounter. Afterward, take your time along the waterfront and near the pier, where local fishermen jig for squid, which is a large part of this town's charm.

Encounters in Pintuyan use no feeding and no bait. Whale sharks are left to rise near the surface naturally, so sightings are never guaranteed, but when you do see one it looks much closer to wild behavior.

Whale sharks gather where the water turns brown from many small crustaceans, and experienced spotters read these signs to find them. One traveler reported meeting four whale sharks, 5–6 m long, during a
30 minutes
encounter.
Feeding, baiting and touching are prohibited. Boats cut their engines as they approach, swimmers keep about
from the whale shark, and flash photography is not allowed. These rules keep the animals safe and the town's tourism sustainable, so please cooperate with your guide.
Registration is at the tourism office in the municipal hall, and boats leave from the beach in Son-ok village. There are no big resorts, just small guesthouses and eateries in a modest town.
Outside the season, or before and after your encounter, jigging for pygmy squid at the port is popular. According to one traveler, sunset squid jigging costs about
, and you can grill your catch at the night market.

At Tagbak Marine Park you can see clear water and sea turtles, and marine sanctuaries such as Napantao are known for snorkeling and diving. They are good alternatives on days when you miss the whale sharks.
At a seminar in Bohol in March 2025, the Donsol and Pintuyan model was presented as community-based whale shark tourism without feeding. As visitor numbers grow, following the rules matters more.

items.title: Basic 2-day, 1-night plan
items.subtitle: Encounter on the afternoon after arrival

children.text: Travel from Tacloban, Surigao or Bohol, arrive in Pintuyan and drop your bags at your lodging. Getting here takes at least half a day, so rest on the first day.
Walk the town pier and night market, and enjoy squid jigging or a seafood dinner. Ask the tourism office in the municipal hall in advance which time slot you want.
Confirm your group and schedule at the tourism office and fill out the forms and waiver. Arriving about
15 minutes
early is a good idea.
Pay at the hut on Son-ok beach, receive a safety briefing and set out by boat. The encounter takes about
3 hours
, and one traveler said staff recommended an afternoon departure.
When a whale shark is found, enter the water on the spotter's signal and observe while following the rules. Rinse off on return, then take an evening bus or move on to your next destination.

Whale sharks may be fewer early and late in the season, so leave some slack in your schedule. If you only have one day, you can arrive early in the morning, finish registration and take an afternoon boat, but encounters may be canceled in bad weather.

The whale shark season usually starts in October or November and runs through late May. The 2026 season closed on June 1 and was announced to reopen in October of the same year. News reports say whale sharks stay from November to April.

Whale sharks are wild, so there is no guarantee on any given day. News reports say they stay from November to April, but we could not confirm daily probability statistics. Encounters are suspended during the rainy and monsoon season.

Small inns cluster in town and near the pier. D&G Transient House, recommended by one traveler, costs about ₱1,200 for two and ₱1,800 for four with rooftop views but no full restaurant, and CM Tourist Inn was said to be fine for a night. Rooms fill up quickly in season, so contact them in advance.

Meals are in town restaurants and at the night market. Grilled squid and local seafood are typical, and there is a beachfront karaoke bar. There are no large malls, so bring cash, toiletries and some snacks.

Nights come early in this village, but travelers sometimes gather at the beachfront karaoke bar. On weekends and holidays in season, restaurants can get crowded, so once your encounter is set, arrange meals and lodging too. It also helps to ask your lodging whether wet gear can be dried after the encounter.
Registration is at the tourism office in the municipal hall. You must fill out forms and a waiver, so arrive about 15 minutes early.
You can rent snorkel and fins at a shop in Son-ok village, but sizes may be limited, so bringing your own is better.
Leave at least two days in case you miss the sharks. One traveler booked four nights.
Use sunscreen that is gentler on corals and the sea, and wear a rash guard to block the sun.
Do not make sudden movements near a whale shark, and enter and leave the water on the spotter's signal.
Turn off the flash and do not use selfie sticks.
Outside boats that break the rules can be banned. Avoid private boats and use official ones.
Bring plenty of cash. ATMs and card payment may be limited.
You will need to shower and change after the encounter, so pack spare clothes and a towel in a waterproof bag.
Whale sharks are wild animals, so you may not see one. Feeding, touching and approaching closely are prohibited, and violators may be restricted from using the service.
Feeding, baiting and touching are prohibited. The distance rule is given as about 3–4 m depending on the source, so follow local instructions.
Some sources mention a limit of six visitors per whale shark and an encounter of no more than five minutes, so confirm the local rules.
Bad weather can cancel an encounter, so leave room in your schedule.
Scuba diving is reportedly not allowed during whale shark encounters. Confirm locally whether only snorkeling or freediving is permitted.
The prices and season information here are based on 2026 traveler reports and news and may change. Check the latest announcements.
The bay stretching out from Pintuyan has many diving and snorkeling spots. It is a good place for ocean activities even outside the whale shark season.
